scope: Proposition 4.1 (Prediction of a tagged packet sum) of the manuscript “A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum” (preprints/A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with-simple-Lebesgue-spectrum-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 144 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0a6684b31440fc6b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be an intermediate map, expressed in a fixed physical volume-preserving coordinate chart. Let Fr = X m∈Mr Ar,m(u, a) e(mθ), F = X r Fr, be a finite list of colors of smooth packets supported compactly in the good arc. Suppose that the finite sets Mr ⊂ Z \ {0} are pairwise disjoint, that |Ar,m(u, a)| is independent of a, and that the list is invariant under complex conjugation: Fr∗ = Fr. In particular, F is real. Let pr be the corresponding spectral densities, put p = P r pr, and suppose that Z T p(z) dz ≤ 3 2 . Assign constants br ∈ C satisfying br∗ = br. Given ε, τ, κ > 0 and any neighborhood of the physical map and its inverse in the smooth topology, there are a finite sequence of passages, a final intermediate map S′, final packets F′ r, and a smooth function Ψ : T → C, such that X r ∥F′ r − Fr∥2 < ε, (4.1) Z T q p′(z) dz ≥ Z T q p(z) dz − τ, p′ = X r p′ r, (4.2) X r brF′ r − Ψ(US′ ) X r F′ r 2 < ε. (4.3) Here the differences in (4.1) are measured in the original physical L2 space. All the physical maps and their inverses can be kept in the prescribed neighborhood. The final good arc I′ satisfies |T\I′| < κ. The output colors again have disjoint nonzero angular-index sets, moduli independent of the spare coordinate, and conjugation symmetry. The multiplier can be chosen with Ψ(−z) = Ψ(z).
